mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (home-country notarization → competent home-country authenticating authority → Embassy/Consulate General of Viet Nam → Department of Consular Affairs, MOFA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory name-based screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives and authorized signatories against (i) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list, (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, (iii) the EU and UK consolidated asset-freeze lists, (iv) Vietnamese national terror-financing and security designations maintained by the State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) and the Ministry of Public Security, and (v) domestic and international PEP registers including immediate family members and known close associates; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandated for any PEP relationship under Law No. 14/2022/QH15 arts. 11–12; continuous re-screening is required at least every six months and upon any material ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal of Viet Nam (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) — https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn, operated by the Business Registration Agency under the Ministry of Planning and Investment; local lodgement with the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province where the head office is situated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Law No. 59/2020/QH14 art. 38 and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, the registered name of a limited liability company must be composed in Vietnamese script and follow the structure: legal-form indicator ('Công ty trách nhiệm hữu hạn' or 'TNHH') plus a proper name of at least two Vietnamese syllables written in Vietnamese orthography. A foreign-language name may be displayed only in parentheses as a direct translation of the Vietnamese name and may not replace the Vietnamese statutory name. Foreign brand names must be transliterated phonetically into Vietnamese script; numerals, symbols and diacritical marks are permitted only where not misleading or non-compliant with the registration system's character set. The Vietnamese name, foreign name and abbreviated name must all appear consistently on the Enterprise Registration Certificate, the company seal and official correspondence.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to an already-registered domestic or foreign-invested enterprise

Names identical to the names of Vietnamese state agencies, armed forces units, political organizations, executive bodies or public authorities (e.g., 'Quốc hội', 'Chính phủ', 'Ủy ban nhân dân', 'Bộ', 'Công an', 'Quân đội')

Tokens implying a licensed banking, payment, securities, insurance or other conditional financial activity without prior approval, including 'Ngân hàng' (bank), 'Thanh toán' (payment), 'Chứng khoán' (securities), 'Bảo hiểm' (insurance), which require written clearance from the State Bank of Viet Nam and/or the relevant ministry before registration
Foreign-language-only proper names, pure foreign-script designators, and names using symbols, punctuation or words contrary to national security, social order or traditional morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 3 working days of dossier lodgement, the provincial DPI must issue or refuse the Enterprise Registration Certificate. Where the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may: (i) refile the same dossier with a corrected name at no additional statutory registration charge; (ii) file a written administrative complaint with the Director of the provincial DPI under the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13 within 30 days of rejection, which must be resolved within 15 working days; (iii) if the complaint is dismissed, appeal to the Ministry of Planning and Investment's Business Registration Agency or initiate administrative proceedings before the provincial People's Court; and (iv) simultaneously reserve an alternative compliant name for 30 days while the administrative appeal is pending. Foreign investors should coordinate the pre-clearance of the name with the parallel Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) application, since the conditional business line (ISIC 6619, payment intermediary services) requires SBV clearance and may trigger an inter-agency name-confidentiality review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the licensed payment-intermediary activity. Decree No. 52/2024/ND-CP and SBV licensing practice require a genuine, physically occupied head office in Viet Nam with a valid lease of at least 12 months remaining, full-time local staff, local bookkeeping, server or systems presence sufficient to evidence real commercial substance, and a registered address consistent with the Enterprise Registration Certificate. A virtual office, co-working mailbox-only address, or registered-agent-only arrangement is insufficient to secure the SBV Payment Intermediary Service licence or to pass the post-incorporation physical verification of the cross-border payment gateway business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High and quantified: approximately 100% probability of a pre-licensing physical verification of the registered head office by the provincial DPI and SBV inspectors; estimated >80% probability of an unannounced on-site SBV inspection within the first 12 months after the payment-intermediary licence is granted; thereafter, statutory annual on-site AML/CFT inspections and ad hoc spot checks by the State Bank of Viet Nam and the Ministry of Public Security are routine for high-risk ISIC 6619 operators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises of Viet Nam No. 59/2020/QH14, notably Articles 22, 24, 25 and 26 (enterprise registration, charter validity and charter capital), Articles 44-55 (limited liability company with two or more members, including the Members' Council) and Articles 57-64 (one-member LLC); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 31-39 (investment registration procedure for foreign investors); Law on Payment No. 09/2024/QH15 and Decree No. 101/2012/ND-CP as amended by Decree No. 80/2016/ND-CP (pre-conditions and licensing of non-bank payment intermediaries); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Agency for Business Registration, Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI), together with the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or central-affiliated city where the registered office is situated, operating the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn); investment registration is handled by the DPI or the Management Board of an Export Processing Zone/Industrial Zone if the office is hosted therein.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giay de nghi dang ky doanh nghiep) in the statutory form I-1, accompanied by the Company Charter (form I-2) and Member List (form I-4); concurrently or sequentially, the Application for Investment Registration Certificate (Giay de nghi cap Giay chung nhan dang ky dau tu) where the investor is foreign, all filed through the National Business Registration Portal or the National Investment Registration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Law on Enterprises 59/2020/QH14 imposes no universal minimum charter capital for an LLC. However, because the entity will operate as a non-bank payment intermediary, the State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) regime requires a paid-up charter capital of at least VND 50 billion (approx. USD 2,050,000) for the license to provide intermediary payment services, including payment gateway services. The capital must be maintained in a blocked bank account opened at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam, fully contributed within 90 days from the date the Enterprise Registration Certificate is issued, and evidenced by a bank certificate of capital availability in the SBV licensing dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 01/2025 OF THE MEMBERS' COUNCIL OF [COMPANY NAME VIET NAM] CO., LTD. ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF ALL MEMBERS ON [●] 2025 AT THE COMPANY'S HEAD OFFICE, PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 55 OF THE LAW ON ENTERPRISES NO. 59/2020/QH14 AND ARTICLES [●] OF THE COMPANY CHARTER. NOW THEREFORE, THE MEMBERS' COUNCIL RESOLVES: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ESCROW. The charter capital of the Company is hereby fixed at VND [●] (in words: Vietnamese Dong [●]), fully subscribed and allocated among the Members as set out in the annexed subscribed capital schedule. The General Director is authorized and directed to open a designated blocked capital account at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam, to receive all capital contributions, to obtain a bank certificate of capital availability for the State Bank of Viet Nam licensing application, and to require each Member to contribute its subscribed capital in full not later than ninety (90) days from the issuance date of the Enterprise Registration Certificate. Any defaulting Member shall be dealt with under Article 26 of the Law on Enterprises, including mandatory adjustment or withdrawal of membership. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company is adopted at [street address, ward, district, province/city], Viet Nam, as stated in the Charter and the enterprise registration application. The Chairman of the Members' Council is authorized to execute the lease, to obtain the lessor's written consent for enterprise registration purposes, and to procure the Company name plate and registered office signage required by Article 11 of the Law on Enterprises and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following Officers are appointed with immediate effect: (a) [●] as Chairman of the Members' Council, who shall be the legal representative of the Company before all third parties and in judicial or arbitral proceedings; (b) [●] as General Director/Chief Executive Officer, vested with authority to conduct day-to-day management, to execute merchant acquiring agreements and card scheme agreements, to open and operate bank accounts, and to apply for and maintain all licenses from the State Bank of Viet Nam, the Ministry of Public Security and other Vietnamese authorities; (c) [●] as Chief Financial Officer, responsible for statutory accounting, tax filings and the escrow capital account; and (d) [●] as Chief Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer, designated under SBV Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN, responsible for AML/CFT policies. The Chairman and the General Director shall jointly hold transaction signature authority in accordance with the Signatory Matrix annexed to this Resolution. 4. GOVERNANCE AND COMPLIANCE MANDATE. The fiscal year is the calendar year. The Company shall appoint an independent audit firm registered in Viet Nam. The General Director is expressly mandated to submit the SBV license application for intermediary payment services (payment gateway), to procure all required insurance, to register the Company's accounts with the Visa and Mastercard networks as a payment facilitator, and to comply with all data-localization, AML and prudential requirements. 5. GENERAL PROVISIONS. Each member may execute this Resolution in counterparts. This Resolution is effective upon adoption and shall be filed with the Company's minute book and registered with the competent DPI as part of the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization, Apostille and Notarization of Founder Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vietnamese Notary Public Office in the province of the registered office; Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam (Consular Department) or competent court for apostille/consular legalization of foreign public documents; Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate abroad where consular legalization is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each foreign corporate member, obtain an apostille or consular legalization of the certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing and audited financial statements of the last two years (Viet Nam is a state party to the Hague Apostille Convention effective 25 October 2023). Arrange a notarized Vietnamese translation of every foreign document. The Vietnamese translations must be certified by a Vietnamese notary or the translation must be enclosed with the original. Prepare notarized copies of passports of the legal representative, the General Director and all members. Ensure all documents bear a date of issue within the most recent three months for certificates of good standing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the foreign investor (apostilled or consular legalized)
Audited financial statements of the foreign investor for the last two years, or a parent guarantee letter
Charter and resolution of the foreign investor authorizing the investment and appointing the Vietnamese representatives
Power of attorney for local lodgment agent, notarized
Passport copies of the proposed legal representative, General Director and compliance officers
Lease agreement or letter of intent for the registered office with lessor consent
Notarized Vietnamese translation of all foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the consular authority raises a query, cure the deficiency within 10 days by supplying a corrected set, re-notarization or supplementary translation; if a certificate of good standing is stale, obtain a new certificate from the home registry; if apostille chain is incomplete, complete the hierarchy of certification (notary + apostille) and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI); if the office is located inside an export processing or industrial zone, the Management Board of the Export Processing Zone/Industrial Zone; submission via the National Investment Registration System and in person at the one-stop shop.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the statutory application for an Investment Registration Certificate in the name of the foreign investor covering the project 'cross-border payment gateway and merchant acquiring services'. Describe the project scope in ISIC 6619 terms and identify the conditional investment status under the Law on Payment and Decree 101/2012/ND-CP. Submit the investor's legal status documents, the financial proof of capital capacity (at least VND 50 billion), the project proposal outlining the payment switching infrastructure hosted in Viet Nam, and the planned location. The DPI will verify the investor's compliance with market-access conditions; if the project falls under SBV conditional licensing, the DPI may consult the SBV before approving the IRC.
required_dossiers: Application for Investment Registration Certificate (statutory form)
Apostilled/legalized and notarized constituent documents of the foreign investor
Proof of financial capability: audited financial statements or parent guarantee covering the charter capital
Project proposal describing the payment gateway activity, technical architecture, data-localization plan and staffing
Certificate of land or lease intention for the registered office address
Draft implementation schedule and capital contribution plan
Power of attorney for the authorized representative submitting the dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a written request for amendment or additional documents, submit the revised dossier within the stated grace period (normally 30 days). If the IRC is refused, file a complaint with the MPI, or institute administrative proceedings before the provincial People's Court in accordance with the Law on Denunciation and the Law on Administrative Procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) Issuance for the Limited Liability Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office of the provincial DPI, acting through the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) and the nationwide one-stop-shop mechanism.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of receiving the IRC, lodge the e-application for enterprise registration. Attach the Company Charter with the full names, addresses and contributed capital of each member, the Member List (form I-4), and the IRC. Select the 'limited liability company with two or more members' / 'one-member LLC' form by capitalization. Confirm the registered office and the legal representative. The Business Registration Office shall examine the dossier for statutory validity of the name, the charter compliance and the capital contribution schedule. The ERC constitutes the certificate of incorporation and triggers automatic tax registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Registration (form I-1)
Company Charter (form I-2) duly notarized
Member List (form I-4) with notarized ID copies of members
Valid Investment Registration Certificate
Notarized copies of the legal representative's ID/passport
Copy of the lease agreement or certificate of legal use of the registered office
Written consent of the lessor to use the address for enterprise registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is queried, the Business Registration Office provides an electronic notice of deficiencies; cure the deficiencies and resubmit within the statutory 30-day window. If the ERC application is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the Director of the DPI and thereafter to the provincial People's Court; incorrect entries can also be corrected through the separate procedure for amendment of enterprise registration content.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Formalization: Corporate Seal, Tax Identification, Publicity and Blocked Capital Contribution Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Business Registration Portal for seal sample notification; General Department of Taxation (eTax / national tax identification system); a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam for the blocked escrow capital account; social insurance authority for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the ERC, manufacture the corporate seal in accordance with Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP and submit an electronic notification of the seal specimen to the National Business Registration Portal. Confirm the automatic tax identification number (TIN) and register the electronic tax payment system. Publish required charter details on the National Business Registration Portal. Open the dedicated blocked capital account at a licensed bank, deposit the charter capital contributions, and obtain the bank certificate of capital availability required for the SBV payment license. Complete the employer registration with the Vietnam Social Security agency. The capital must be fully paid within 90 days of ERC issuance.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Certificate of the corporate seal specimen and the seal notification confirmation from the portal
Tax identification number registration (automatic via ERC; supplementary file if needed)
Charter and list of members for bank KYC
Passport/ID of legal representative and authorized bank signatories
Resolution of the Members' Council approving the blocked account and banking mandate
Proof of registered office for bank verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal notification is rejected, correct the electronic form and resubmit within 24 hours; if the tax number is not automatically integrated, file a written request with the local Tax Department and obtain a confirmation; if the bank refuses the escrow account, address KYC queries by providing updated corporate documents and enhanced due diligence information, or select an alternative licensed commercial bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-license Condition Filing with the State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) for Intermediary Payment Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Bank of Viet Nam, Payment Department (and non-bank credit institution supervision units) in Ha Noi; technical inspection and on-site verification of the payment gateway infrastructure.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the ERC is issued and before commencing merchant acquiring operations, submit the application for the License to Provide Intermediary Payment Services (payment gateway category) to the SBV. Demonstrate compliance with the capital condition (paid-up charter capital of at least VND 50 billion), the technical infrastructure requirement that core switching and processing systems are physically located in Viet Nam, the IT security standards, the AML/CFT compliance program under Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN, and the two-year clean record requirement. Include the card scheme participation evidence (Visa/Mastercard principal or principal-eligibility documentation), the merchant acquiring risk management framework, and the operational continuity plan. The SBV may conduct an on-site inspection of the registered office and the data facility before issuing the license.
required_dossiers: Application for the license to provide intermediary payment services (SBV statutory form)
Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate
Bank certificate confirming the blocked capital account balance of at least VND 50 billion
Business plan covering payment gateway operations, cross-border flows and foreign currency rules
Technical architecture description with in-country data hosting contracts
AML/CFT policies, internal control manual and designation of the Chief AML Officer
Organizational chart and qualifications of the legal representative, General Director and compliance staff
Draft agreements with card networks and acquiring partners
Statement of no credit institution license revocation or no enforcement record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SBV requests amendments or further verifications, respond in writing within the prescribed deadline and supply the supplementary evidence; if the license is refused, the applicant may file a petition for reconsideration with the SBV Governor and subsequently an administrative lawsuit; any denial must state the legal grounds, and the applicant may correct the omissions and file a fresh application after not less than 3 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) for the payment services license; Ministry of Public Security / Provincial Fire Police for fire safety; Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) and the provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) for environmental registration; Ministry of Information and Communications for data center and information security compliance insofar as the gateway infrastructure is concerned.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: License to Provide Intermediary Payment Services (Giay phep hoat dong cung ung dich vu trung gian thanh toan) issued by the State Bank of Viet Nam, with supplemental registration as an entity providing payment gateway services in the Visa and Mastercard networks.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) - General Department of Environment; in delegation, the provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) where the registered office and server facility are located.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Environmental Registration (Dang ky moi truong) for an office-based electronic payment services operation with domestic wastewater and electronic waste only; a Full EIA Report is not mandatorily required for an ISIC 6619 payment gateway where the annual wastewater volume does not exceed 100 m3/day and no hazardous industrial production is undertaken, but the Provincial Environmental Registration Certificate remains obligatory before operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with QCVN 40:2011/BTNMT (national technical regulation on industrial wastewater, Column B: pH 5.5-9, BOD5 not exceeding 50 mg/L, COD not exceeding 150 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 100 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 60 mg/L); QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT and QCVN 20:2009/BTNMT (industrial emissions and VOC thresholds; total VOC not exceeding 600 mg/m3 at the exhaust point for any standby generators); hazardous waste management under Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP with environmental manifests and transfer to licensed treatment facilities; the electronic waste (WEEE) handling plan and, where applicable, registration of scrap import or disposal under Decree 08/2022. Backup generator emissions must satisfy QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT limits and noise standards under QCVN 26:2016/BTNMT.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (or Certificate of Fire Safety Eligibility) and written acceptance of fire protection design under Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP for the office premises and the server/control room; structural load verification certificate confirming the floor load capacity for server racks, UPS systems and cooling equipment in compliance with QCVN 06:2021/BXD; workplace occupational safety verification under the Labor Code (Law No. 45/2019/QH14), including employee health examinations, safety training and registration of high-risk equipment; civil defense registration as an administrative/IT facility under Decree No. 74/2012/ND-CP if the workforce is at or above 500 persons; for data processing, the SBV technical inspection confirming that core payment switching and processing systems are located within the territory of Viet Nam, supported by an information security incident response and business continuity clearance acceptable to the SBV.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT) of the Ministry of Finance, Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; taxpayer portal at etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; National Business Registration Portal at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; electronic invoice portal at hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested limited liability company must first obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial investment authority or export processing zone authority, and thereafter an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) through the National Business Registration Portal. The enterprise code stated on the ERC serves as the automatic tax identification number (MST) and is simultaneously registered with the GDT for corporate income tax and VAT. A separate GDT tax-code registration is required for any branch, additional establishment, or VAT registration for non-resident foreign contractor services. A non-resident foreign supplier of cross-border digital services must register through the GDT eTax portal and be issued a foreign-supplier tax identity before filing returns; if no direct registration is feasible, a local withholding agent must be appointed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not operate a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch classification regime. An LLC may elect its constitutive ownership structure (single-member or multi-member), its applicable accounting framework (Vietnamese Accounting Standards, with IFRS only for group consolidation or statutory banking/licensed payment-services preparers), and its investment incentive status, including optional certification as an export processing enterprise (EPE). The Foreign Contractor Tax regime provides a deemed-output tax mechanism for non-resident suppliers but does not create pass-through entity classification for Viet Nam domestic LLCs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (value added tax; thuế giá trị gia tăng)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 100,000,000 annual turnover from taxable supplies. Domestic enterprises, including foreign-invested LLCs, are VAT-registered without a turnover threshold, whereas the VND 100 million low-turnover threshold applies to household businesses and, critically, to non-resident foreign digital-service suppliers in the GDT foreign-supplier registration process for cross-border digital supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing became mandatory in Viet Nam on 1 July 2022. Every VAT invoice generated by an established business must be transmitted to the GDT electronic-invoice system in XML format within one working day of issue; GDT either validates the invoice or assigns a live invoice serial code and corporate hash code. Point-of-sale or cash-register-connected transactions, and specific supervised transactions, require real-time transmission to GDT before delivery/completion using authorised fiscal-cash-register data connections. An e-invoice must include a machine-readable QR code and satisfy the XML data layout in Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. For payment-processing service providers, invoice issuance must be integrated through the GDT e-invoice application API or a certified third-party e-invoice service provider; customs exports are cleared electronically through the VNACCS/VCIS data interchange, not on paper.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Viet Nam-based LLC may apply the 0% VAT rate to exported goods if the goods physically leave Viet Nam customs territory, are sold under a written export contract, have an accepted customs export declaration, and are transported to a foreign buyer or to an export processing enterprise under EPE-qualifying conditions. For the cross-border payment-gateway scope, a zero rating is available only for services supplied to a foreign organisation or individual that are consumed entirely outside Viet Nam; international acquiring, routing, clearing, and settlement services supplied to a non-resident merchant for card transactions occurring wholly outside Viet Nam can qualify, if the Vietnam-based PSP maintains contractual evidence, non-resident invoicing, and operational records demonstrating offshore consumption. Domestic acquiring fees, gateway fees on Vietnam-origin transactions, merchant setup fees, and processing margins attributable to Viet Nam remain subject to 10% VAT (or the reduced rate for currently eligible sectors); VAT-exempt supplies cannot be zero-rated and VAT refunds are allowed only where input VAT exceeds output VAT and the taxpayer has qualifying export turnover.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic VNACCS acknowledgment with accepted status)
Bill of Lading (or airway bill/multimodal transport document showing physical egress from Vietnamese customs territory)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed bank in Viet Nam evidencing foreign-currency repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: GDT and customs authorities cross-match e-invoice data, VNACCS export declarations, bank SWIFT/FX payment records, and Inward Remittance Certificates during post-clearance audits. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims trigger clawback of the VAT refund, imposition of late-payment interest at 0.02% per day, and administrative penalties from one to three times the under-refunded tax amount under the Law on Tax Administration 38/2019/QH14, as amended. Knowingly issuing false customs declarations, using fraudulent transport documents, or abusing export-claim arrangements to illegally obtain tax refunds may constitute tax evasion under Penal Code Article 200, with individual criminal liability of up to 7 years' imprisonment and corporate entity-level fines up to VND 4.5 billion, suspension of operations, and revocation of the payment-service licence. No statutory limitation applies where fraud is demonstrated, and retrospective clawbacks may extend to the entire VAT refund principal plus statutory interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) — Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam; the FX regulator is the Foreign Exchange Administration Department under the SBV, exercising delegated authority pursuant to the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 06/2005/PL-UBTVQH11, as amended by Ordinance No. 06/2013/UBTVQH13.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vietnam operates a partial-convertibility regime. Current-account transactions (trade in goods and services, profit remittances, interest, royalties, scheme fees and operating expenses) are generally convertible and may be settled freely through SBV-licensed banks without a prior exchange-control permit, provided the underlying documentation is presented and the transaction is economically real. Capital-account transactions remain controlled: FDI equity must be injected through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed bank; cross-border borrowings by the VN_LLC require SBV registration under Circular 08/2022/TT-NHNN; portfolio investment requires an Indirect Investment Capital Account; and outward investment by Vietnamese entities requires the relevant investment registration certificate. Profit remittance hurdles for the foreign-invested PSP are material: annual after-tax profits may be remitted abroad in USD or EUR through the DICA only after (i) the annual audited financial statements have been prepared, (ii) corporate income tax finalization has been filed with the tax authority, (iii) the statutory profit-remittance notice has been lodged with the competent tax office, and (iv) all conditions relating to registered foreign loans and outstanding SBV registrations have been satisfied. In practice, the receiving bank requires a tax-compliance confirmation, an unqualified audit opinion, and evidence of accumulated distributable retained earnings before executing the dividend remittance; the absence of any one of these items is the most frequent operational blocker.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a Vietnamese exporting entity, all foreign-currency proceeds from the sale of goods or services must be repatriated into a foreign-currency account held with an SBV-licensed authorized bank within 90 days from the date of customs clearance of exports or, for service exports, within 90 days from the date of service completion and invoicing (Circular 03/2019/TT-NHNN, as amended). No general mandatory conversion ratio applies to commercial exporters today: the historical export-proceeds surrender obligations have been abolished, and the VN_LLC is entitled to retain 100% of its export proceeds in its onshore foreign-currency account and to convert them at negotiated bank rates. Mandatory sale to the SBV is limited to designated state budget revenues, crude oil, and natural gas receipts. For this payment gateway, cross-border acquiring, clearing, scheme and processing fees earned from foreign merchants constitute service exports; 100% of those earnings must be credited to the PSP's onshore foreign-currency account at a licensed bank and may not be netted, offset, or retained offshore.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) + USD/VND Operational Account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Operation Report (Vietnamese: Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động của doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province/city where the LLC's registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 January of each calendar year; the first report is due after the enterprise's first full year of registration and every 30 January thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 10,000,000–20,000,000 under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP for late or omitted filing; persistent non-filing may lead DPI to propose revocation of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Fee remittance and declaration (Vietnamese: Lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Authority (Cục Thuế) under the General Department of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 January of the current year; newly registered enterprises are exempt from the license fee for the first calendar year of establishment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount; administrative penalties ranging from VND 2,000,000 to VND 5,000,000 for failure to declare; prolonged non-payment may trigger tax enforcement measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return (Vietnamese: Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Authority (Cục Thuế) under the General Department of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 90 days after the fiscal year end, i.e., by 31 March for a calendar-year entity; adjusted to the next working day if the statutory date falls on a public holiday.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP up to VND 50,000,000 depending on delay; additional late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; underpayment penalties of up to 20% of under-declared CIT; serious tax evasion may lead to criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and audit report (foreign-invested enterprise mandatory audited financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Authority, Business Registration Office (DPI), and Provincial Statistical Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of the fiscal year end, i.e., by 31 March for a calendar-year entity; audited financial statements must accompany the annual CIT finalization dossier of the foreign-invested LLC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties under Decree 41/2018/ND-CP for late or non-submission of audited financial statements, generally VND 10,000,000–20,000,000; false audit records may result in additional sanctions and re-audit orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payment Intermediary Operation and Compliance Report under the SBV payment service licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Payment System Department, State Bank of Vietnam (SBV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of the fiscal year end, or on the exact date specified in the payment intermediary licence; normally submitted with audited financial statements and the annual AML/CFT report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SBV enforcement fines, potentially up to VND 80,000,000, for reporting violations; repeated or severe breaches may lead to suspension or revocation of the payment service licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold applies to this LLC. A mandatory independent audit is required for all foreign-invested enterprises in Viet Nam and for all licensed non-bank payment service providers under the Law on Enterprises 2020 and SBV payment intermediary regulations. The audit must be performed by an independent audit firm permitted by the Ministry of Finance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS) as prescribed by Law on Accounting 2015 and Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; statutory financial statements must be prepared in Vietnamese Dong and follow the Vietnamese chart of accounts. IFRS may be used only for supplemental or parent-group reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Viet Nam does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing to DPI. However, any change in member ownership, indirect ownership, or beneficial control must be recorded in the LLC's member register and reported in the enterprise registration record within 10 days of the change. Under Decree 05/2019/ND-CP and SBV AML/CFT requirements, the payment gateway LLC must maintain current beneficial-ownership identification files and make them available to SBV and tax authorities upon request; no annual UBO filing is submitted unless triggered by a licensing or audit request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors/General Director and legal representatives with appointment details
Minute Book containing Member Council resolutions and General Director decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–1,400 per annum in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City for registered office, filing agent, and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–10,000 per annum for a licensed statutory audit of a payment gateway LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific statutory holiday applies to payment gateway/PSP activities. A qualified enterprise applying high-technology or new-incentive criteria may obtain CIT rates of 10%–15% for up to 15 years, but such treatment is not ordinarily available to ISIC 6619 merchant acquirers without separate investment certificate approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly provisional CIT declaration – Form 01/TNDN filed electronically via the Vietnamese e-tax portal (HTKK / iTaxViewer, portal: thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 30th day of the first month following each calendar quarter (e.g., Q1 filing by 30 April).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer name, tax code, address, fiscal year, tax official to contact.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested LLC must identify the Vietnamese license number and overseas shareholder tax residence code for treaty monitoring.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Stated revenue, deductible expenses, projected taxable income and CIT payable for the quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border payment gateway, quarterly estimates must be based on Vietnam-sourced processing fees and merchant discount income only, with no transfer pricing adjustments at the estimation stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable reduced by prior quarter prepayments and parent company tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot offset foreign taxes against Vietnamese CIT in a provisional filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fines from VND 2 million to VND 25 million, depending on lateness; overdue tax interest accrues at 0.03% per day on unpaid amounts; repeated non-filing may result in provisional assessment and license suspension.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT finalization return – Form 03/TNDN filed electronically via the e-tax portal (HTKK / iTaxViewer, portal: thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 90th day from the end of the fiscal year (31 March for calendar-year taxpayers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenue derived from carrying on business, including merchant acquiring, clearing, interchange, setup fees and terminal/API-related fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident gateway must include only Vietnam-sourced revenue; fees invoiced to offshore affiliates are reportable but are subject to TP adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual expenses related to revenue, limited to the Law on CIT deduction rules; includes personnel, depreciation, commission, communication, and outsourced processing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore head-office charges require valid contracts, separate invoices, written identification and arm's-length proof; non-deductible if no actual service is rendered in Vietnam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A1 minus deductible expenses plus other assessable income, reduced by exempt income and carryforward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border branch/LLC must apply the 5-year CIT loss carryforward; any unrelieved foreign losses are not claimed on the Vietnam return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory corporate income tax rate applied to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard rate is 20%; no reduced rate should be claimed unless the PSP has a valid investment certificate for a preferential sector.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line E1 – Credit for foreign taxes and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit (where DTA provides), withholding taxes already settled, and quarterly prepayments credited against final CIT liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Vietnamese LLC cannot credit foreign corporate tax of shareholders; only Vietnamese withheld taxes and approved DTA credits on Vietnam-source income may be credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT payable after prepayments and credits, or refundable excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any excess withheld foreign contractor tax (FCT) on payments to the LLC is refundable only through annual finalization procedures with documentary evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late finalization return: administrative fine of VND 2–25 million plus interest at 0.03%/day. If underpaid CIT is discovered, penalties can be up to 20% of underpaid tax for late payment and up to 100%–300% for fraudulent under-declaration (Decree 125/2020/ND-CP).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Vietnam does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax on outbound dividends; dividends are distributed from after-tax CIT earnings, and a foreign LLC member receiving dividends is not subject to further Vietnamese tax at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Dividends: no Vietnamese DTA relief procedure is required because no source withholding exists. For interest and royalties, the foreign payee must submit to the Vietnamese payor: (i) a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) from the shareholder’s or lender’s tax authority; (ii) a Form of DTA claim approved by the General Department of Taxation if the rate change exceeds de minimis thresholds; and (iii) evidence that the recipient is the beneficial owner. The payor must file a foreign contractor withholding tax declaration (Form 01/FCWT) and obtain approval before applying the reduced treaty rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory foreign contractor withholding is deemed CIT of 10% and deemed VAT of 5%, aggregate 15% on gross royalty, reducible under DTA to typically 10% CIT (e.g., Singapore, Korea, Japan). Interest: statutory deemed CIT rate is 5% on gross interest, no VAT; most DTAs cap interest withholding at 10%, and certain treaties reduce to 0% for bank loan interest. Rates are governed by Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC and specific DTA schedules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required when annual related-party transaction value equals or exceeds VND 50 billion. Master File: required when the ultimate parent group’s annual consolidated global turnover exceeds VND 18 trillion. Country-by-Country reporting applies at the VND 18 trillion group turnover threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP and the anti-abuse provisions of Law on Tax Administration 38/2019/QH14, the tax authority will disregard or recharacterize offshore entities lacking real economic substance. For a cross-border payment gateway, substance is determined by the presence of Vietnamese employees conducting merchant due diligence, transaction monitoring, board decision-making in-country, and operational control. A shell company incorporated only to own IP or booking fees, without functions and risks, will be treated as a façade and profits will be re-attributed to Vietnam.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Vietnam-source processing revenue by recording portion of merchant discount fees through offshore shell entities without substance; issuing false expense invoices or inflating intercompany service fees above arm's-length value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, an administrative fine of 1–3 times the evaded tax amount; interest at 0.03%/day on underpaid amounts until payment. Criminal liability under Penal Code (amended 2017) Article 200 for tax evasion: fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment of up to 5 years, depending on the amount evaded and previous violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers are jointly and severally liable for the full evaded amount if they signed or consciously permitted false returns; Vietnamese courts can order personal civil restitution, a 12-month exit ban, freezing of personal bank accounts, and criminal detention during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a paper holding company in a tax haven solely to earn merchant processing fees from Vietnamese merchants with no staff, office, or decision-making in the claimed residence, then invoking a DTA to reduce or eliminate withholding tax on remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will reject the treaty benefit, reclassify the income as a taxable permanent establishment in Vietnam, impose the 20% CIT and FCT deficiencies, add 20%–100% late-payment penalties and 0.03%/day interest. Penal Code tax evasion provisions can also apply if the structure is found to be a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Vietnamese LLC that knowingly interposed a shell entity can be stripped of limited liability protection; personal liability attaches for unpaid corporate taxes, travel restrictions are imposed, and criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years may be sought for fraudulent bankruptcy or tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting funds from Vietnamese merchants and settling through the LLC’s payment gateway without holding an intermediate payment services license from the State Bank of Vietnam, or operating a cross-border acquiring business outside the scope of the license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The State Bank of Vietnam may issue license-revocation orders, administrative fines under the Non-Cash Payment Law 2023 (No. 23/2023/QH15) and Decree 52/2024/ND-CP, confiscation of illegal remuneration, and suspension of operations for up to 12 months. If criminal threshold is met, prosecution for illegal business under Penal Code Article 200 can result in fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who directed unlicensed payment processing are individual offenders: they can be fined , obligated for restitution of merchant losses, barred from holding senior positions in Vietnamese payment institutions, and, in cases involving multiple merchants, subject to imprisonment from 3 to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform customer due diligence, beneficial owner verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring on high-risk cross-border merchants; allowing shell merchants to launder proceeds through card-not-present acquiring channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Vietnam Anti-Money Laundering Law 2022 (effective 2023) and State Bank guidance up to VND 500 million for licensees; suspension of the PSP license for repeated failure; fully acquitted disgorgement of laundered funds. Criminal liability under Penal Code Article 324 (money laundering) applies up to 10 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the PSP are subject to criminal proceedings if they knowingly processed tainted funds or failed to file Suspicious Transaction Reports; personal fines up to VND 500 million, travel bans, and imprisonment from 5 to 10 years are statutory ceilings. The corporate veil is pierced where AML compliance was deliberately not implemented.
